newsitem.title: JAPAN: Drunken passenger briefly hijacks Japan airliner.
newsitem.headline: Drunken passenger briefly hijacks Japan airliner.

text.p: A drunken passenger wielding a fruit knife briefly hijacked a Japanese domestic airliner on Monday before being overpowered by the crew as he tried to leave the aircraft after it landed, local media reported.

A Tranport Ministry spokesman told Reuters the pilot informed the Fukuoka Airport the aircraft had been hijacked about 10 minutes before the aircraft landed at 6:50 p.m. (0930 GMT) in the southern city of Fukuoka.
The Boeing 777 had completed a one-hour scheduled flight from Itami Airport on the border of Osaka and Hyogo prefectures.
The aircraft was carrying 182 passengers including four children and 10 crew. No one was injured in the incident.

The man, identified by police authorities as Yuichi Yano, a 31-year-old Japanese who was unemployed, was arrested after being overpowered by the crew as he was leaving the aircraft, Fukuoka Prefectural Police said.

Yano, who sat in the front row of the aircraft, entered the cockpit with a 15-cm (12-inch) fruit knife and demanded that when the aircraft landed at Fukuoka it should be refuelled and take off again for an unnamed international airport.
After the plane landed he then told the pilot he wanted to get off the aircraft with the stewardess, and walked out of the cockpit by himself toward the exit, Japanese media reported.
The passengers, who were unaware there was a hijacking in progress, filed off the plane as normal after about a 15-minute delay.
"I didn't know what was happening at all. I didn't realise there was a hijack until we all got off the plane," one male passenger told reporters at the airport.

"I saw the man (hijacker) being overpowered by a lot of people. They were struggling with each other pretty roughly," said another passenger who saw the hijacker being held in custody by the crew before being arrested by the police.

The airport was temporarily closed off but re-opened at 9:00 p.m. (1200 GMT). Four flights were cancelled and four other flights were directed to land at other airports in the vicinity due to the incident, airport officials said.

Yano is currently being questioned by the Fukuoka Airport Police, but police officials said they still do not know why Yano attempted the hijack or how he was able to carry the fruit knife into the aircraft.
Passengers who sat in the first five rows of the aircraft near Yano are also being questioned by the police, but the other passengers had all left the airport, the ANA spokesman said.

The most recent hijack on a domestic flight was by a 54- year-old former Japanese banker, who is currently on trial for hijacking the ANA passenger plane with an awl after it took off from Tokyo's Haneda Airport in June 1995.
Riot police later arrested the hijacker and freed the 364 passengers and crew unhurt.
Last year, the court ordered the hijacker to pay the company 54 million yen in damages in the first civil suit brought by a domestic airline in a hijack case.
All Nippon Airways Co Ltd is Japan's second-largest airline.
